issues.description: The UML in the problem statement specifies Farm.addAnimal(animal: Animal):boolean (i.e., a boolean return type), but the solution implements addAnimal as void (public void addAnimal(Animal animal)) and the template does not declare the method. This creates a return-type mismatch: students following the UML would implement addAnimal to return boolean, which would conflict with the provided solution and likely with hidden tests or the intended starter/template expectations.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signature across artifacts. Either update the UML and problem text to declare addAnimal(animal: Animal):void to match the solution, or change the template and solution to implement addAnimal returning boolean (e.g., public boolean addAnimal(Animal animal) { return animals.add(animal); }) and update tests/instructions accordingly. Prefer updating the UML/problem statement to :void if the pedagogical intent is simply to add the animal without returning a status.
